questions.question: State the approximate percentages of the three most abundant gases in dry air, and explain why water vapour is not included in this list.
questions.expected_answer: Nitrogen about 78%, oxygen about 21%, argon about 0,9%. Water vapour is left out because its amount varies greatly from place to place and time to time (from nearly 0% in cold or desert air to about 3-4% in hot humid air), so composition is given for dry air.

questions.question: Explain why air pressure and air density decrease as altitude increases.
questions.expected_answer: Air has mass and is pulled down by gravity. The air near the surface is compressed by the weight of all the air above it, so its particles are packed closely and it has high density and pressure. Higher up there is less air above pressing down, so the air is less compressed: particles are further apart, density is lower, and pressure (the weight of the air above) is lower.

questions.question: A climber says there is less oxygen on Mount Everest because the air there contains a smaller percentage of oxygen. Correct this statement.
questions.expected_answer: The percentage of oxygen is the same (about 21%) at all heights in the lower atmosphere. The air is less dense, so each breath contains fewer molecules of all gases, including oxygen; at the summit the air pressure is only about a third of that at sea level, so each breath holds about a third as much oxygen.
